# SPECIMEN_01

The document's own parts

Twelve parts, printed at 1:1 where they can stand on a plate and stated where they cannot. Each one carries its contract, its stylesheet and the surface that asks for it.

  • SHEET: VERIFIED

/THE GALLERY

The sheet's own index, before its bands

Sixteen bands, one row each: the sheet's own apparatus, the ten families, the material and the register. Every row states the band, the figure its matrix counted, what it argues and what it is read for - so the frame can be seen before it is read.

# GALLERY   16 BANDS

  1. # 01 /THE SHEET A contact sheet is the one page where equal cells are right: the parts are genuinely equal, and the reader is choosing between them rather than reading them. Every part of the document as one cell, with a printed part linking to its plate and an absent one printing its reason in place of a link. 12 PARTS / 9 PRINTED / 3 ABSENT / 0 FOLDED
  2. # 02 /THE PLATES A plate's stage is 1:1. Nothing on this sheet is scaled to fit: a part that could not be shown at its own size is stated in THE ABSENCES instead. Nine parts are printed and seven of them stand on a plate at 1:1 - a stage that is the surface the part will be printed on, the white insert for a flat part and the creme field for a part that is itself a surface. The other two are printed on the bands they belong to. 9 PRINTED PARTS / 1:1
  3. # 03 /THE ABSENCES An absence is a composition, not a gap: what would be here, why it is not, and where to read the thing itself. The parts that cannot stand on a plate, in the same three rows every absence on this site uses. 3 STATED
  4. # 04 /THE STATES A page without its adverse states is half a page, and the eight words are the whole vocabulary: empty, loading, partial, error, stale, too much, too long, missing. The nine conditions the document's own surfaces survive, composed live, each naming where it happens. 9 CONDITIONS / 8 WORDS
  5. # 05 /THE FIELD A control's states are the design: what it is when it is empty, when it is refused, when it is read-only, and when the reader cannot see it at all. The input family's matrix and its live rows - the fields, the labels, the selects, the toggles and the one control that is a paragraph. 10 × 23 / 230 CELLS / 185 BUILT / 29 ROWS
  6. # 06 /THE OVERLAY An overlay is judged in the two seconds after a click: what it covers, what it returns to, and the five ways out. The overlay family's matrix, its five-rule dismissal contract, and every state printed live - a slip, a drawer, a modal, a menu and a command well. 10 × 20 / 200 CELLS / 144 BUILT / 34 ROWS
  7. # 07 /THE DISPLAY A display is read rather than used: its worst state is not a failed action but a figure that lies about its own extent. The display family's matrix, its verdict on the two components no page mounts, and every state a chart, a calendar, a table or a figure is read in. 19 × 21 / 399 CELLS / 331 BUILT / 44 ROWS
  8. # 08 /THE RECORD A ledger is believed, not used. A fact that has lost its adverse state is a fact that lies, and a lie is the one defect this family cannot survive. The ledger, the matrix, the stage, the well, the figure, the pair, the archive and the register - every form the document states a fact in. 8 × 24 / 192 CELLS / 120 BUILT / 52 ROWS
  9. # 09 /THE NARRATIVE A narrative block is the thing a reader is TOLD: a band opens a subject, a stage explains an order, a figure shows evidence, a well hands over a command, and a failure explains a dead end. The narrative family's matrix, the three behaviours the brief named by hand, and sixty-two rows of bands, stages, figures, wells, transcripts and failures. 15 × 19 / 285 CELLS / 180 BUILT / 62 ROWS
  10. # 10 /THE FRAME The frame decides whether content can be read at all - and its one law is that nothing here is a card: a shell holds tracks, a track holds bands, a band holds records, and a card is a record's surface. The shell, the rail, the seam, the plate and the surface states, plus the five compositions a page shell has to survive - no rail, two rails, a shell inside a shell, a pane pair at 640px, and a plate with no image. 20 × 22 / 440 CELLS / 303 BUILT / 55 ROWS
  11. # 11 /THE READING Furniture fails by losing the reader: a rail that does not say where you are, a contents list that does not say where you are in the page, a folio that does not say how far you have got. The rail, the contents, the index card, the article, the appendix, the folio, the see-also and the leader - a document with one section, with ninety, a heading wider than the rail, and a strip at 640px. 14 × 24 / 336 CELLS / 214 BUILT / 57 ROWS
  12. # 12 /THE COMPOSITION The marketing layer is a LAYER, not a block: thirty-five `Dynamic/*` parts were built to be the schema between content and surface, and a part with no importer is a decision the owner has not made yet. The hero, the bands, the cards, the manifest, the marks, the verdict on every `Dynamic/*` part, and sixty-six live compositions - a hero with no evidence image, a proof band of three, nine tiles in a narrow card, a seal at 16px and at 240px. 58 × 24 / 1392 CELLS / 818 BUILT / 66 ROWS
  13. # 13 /THE SMALL SURFACES A small surface fails by being ABANDONED: the page a reader reaches when they are locked out, their session expired, their request did not send - and the page nobody designed a second state for. The credential frame and its report, the account directory, the licence's clause apparatus, a request route, the reference blocks, and the seven ways these pages are read. 16 × 24 / 384 CELLS / 179 BUILT / 47 ROWS
  14. # 14 /THE APPARATUS Apparatus fails by being absent and unnoticed: a motion that does not fire, a card with no image, a provider that was never configured, a trail with no crumbs - none of them throws, and every one of them is a lie about the state of the world. Motion, the specimen surface's own blocks and this index, the head, the runtime providers, the trail and the blog - the reduced-motion reader, the motion with no trigger, the specimen at one and at forty, the card with no image and the provider with no logo. 17 × 24 / 408 CELLS / 183 BUILT / 50 ROWS
  15. # 15 /THE MATERIAL Six things and no seventh: a seventh colour would be a second identity, and the sheet is where that would show. The paper, the insert, two inks, the one accent and the one hairline - shown rather than described, painted with the token itself. 6 SPECIMENS
  16. # 16 /THE REGISTER A sheet that could disagree with itself would be two claims about one document, so every figure on this page is counted from the table it prints. What the sheet counted and the file it counted from, then the four doors out. 12 PARTS COUNTED

16 bands: 4266 cells of state matrix printed across 496 live rows, plus the sheet's own apparatus, the material and the closing register. Every figure is the family module's own export - a component added to a family moves the row above it in the same edit, and the index cannot claim a count the matrix beside it does not print. The row's `argues` line is the family's question, and its `read` line is what the band prints: a reader who reads only this band has seen the shape of the document. The conditions every matrix asks, and every component's answer to each, are collected on one page: /SPECIMEN/STATES - the term sheet this index is the table of contents for.

Every figure here is the family module's own export, not a number typed beside a label: a component added to `Reading.ts` moves the row above it in the same edit. That is the same rule `/THE REGISTER` follows at the foot of the page, applied to the page's own table of contents.

/THE SHEET

Every part, on one sheet

Twelve cells, one per part: its mark, its name, the layer it belongs to, and what the sheet did with it. A printed part links to its plate; an absent one prints its reason where the plate would be.

# SHEET   12 PARTS

  1. 01 BADGE A word in a Jelly badge, with an optional dot. SURFACE → PRINTED
  2. 02 LABEL A form label that states its own two conditions. FORM → PRINTED
  3. 03 CARD Three sections on one Jelly card. SURFACE → PRINTED
  4. 04 TABLE A head row and one row per record. BLOCK → PRINTED
  5. 05 PROSE One string, parsed into paragraphs. BLOCK → PRINTED
  6. 06 ARTICLE CARD An entry, as a card. CONTENT → PRINTED
  7. 07 PROPERTIES Six claims as records: three kept, three filed. BLOCK → PRINTED
  8. 08 CHIPS A record's states, as chips. SURFACE → PRINTED
  9. 09 TIER TABLE Four tiers and their protocols. CONTENT → PRINTED
  10. 10 HEADER The legacy schema-driven bar. SURFACE ◎ ABSENT
  11. 11 FOOTER The four-column closing band. SURFACE ◎ ABSENT
  12. 12 VERIFICATION Checksums and signatures, with copy. BLOCK ◎ ABSENT

The sheet indexes the document's parts - the gallery above indexes the sheet's bands - and it is the page's adverse state at once: a part that cannot be printed keeps its cell, and the cell says so. 12 cells, 9 of them printed and 3 of them stated.

A sheet is the one page where equal cells are right: the parts are genuinely equal, and the reader is choosing between them rather than reading them.

/THE PLATES

The parts, printed

Seven plates. Each holds one part at its own size on a stage, and each stage is a white insert lying on the field - the same box a record uses, so a part is printed on the surface it will be printed on.

A plate's stage is 1:1. Nothing on this sheet is scaled to fit: a part that could not be shown at its own size is stated in THE ABSENCES instead.

/THE ABSENCES

The parts that are not printed

Three parts cannot stand on a plate, and each says why in the same three rows every absence on this site uses: what would be here, why it is not, and where to read the thing itself.

/THE STATES

What a part has to survive

Nine conditions, composed in the record grammar, each naming the surface where it actually happens. A part without its adverse states is half a part, and a page without them is half a page.

The vocabulary is fixed at eight words, and the legend above prints all eight. A ninth word would be a state the ink register has no tone for.

/THE FIELD

The field, and every state it has

Every condition the family has to hold, against every component that has to hold it: the matrix, with a reason printed in full for every cell that cannot exist, then the family mounted live at the state it is best known by. A field is the one part a reader touches with their hands, so its states are the product.

/THE CONDITIONS15

The fifteen conditions a field has to hold, in the order the state layer names them.

The matrix and the rows read one file: Content/Specimen/Field.ts states every cell's disposition, every row's state and the one line that says when it is right. A state added there appears on both - the matrix's figures and the rows' order - with no second edit, which is the same rule the parts table above follows. This band is not on /THE SHEET and that is a boundary rather than a gap: the sheet indexes the twelve Dynamic parts, one cell and one plate each, and this band is the first one about a family of primitives - ten components whose subject is their states, which a plate holding one part at 1:1 could not print.

A cell that cannot exist carries its reason in the notes rather than a truncated one in the cell, and a state that a printed sheet cannot produce - focus - is declared on the block, so it prints.

/THE OVERLAY

The overlay, and every way out of it

Ten components on one surface, one item grammar and one dismissal contract. The matrix prints every condition against every component with a reason for each cell that cannot exist; the contract prints the five ways a slip is left; and the rows print the states the site had never shown - an empty menu, a disabled row that says why, a submenu three deep, a dialog taller than the viewport, a popover at the right edge, a record with rows it cannot read, a list at a shorter stride, and a slip opened over the card it belongs to.

/THE PANELS15

The four surfaces that take the reader's whole attention: a dialog, a drawer, a sheet, a popover. Each one is a slip with a head, a body and a foot - and each one is printed here in the four states it was never printed in: loading, empty, failed, and outgrown.

#01

READY

DIALOG

Right when the reader must decide before the page continues - a record with a head, a body and one action.

#02

LOADING

DIALOG

Right when the panel is open and its rows have not arrived: the head counts LOADING and the skeleton holds the row pitch.

#03

DIALOG

Right when the action the panel opened for was cut off - STATUS, cause, next step and the retry, in that order.

#04

DIALOG

Right when the set the panel opened on holds nothing: what would be here, why it is not, and the way out.

#05

DIALOG

Right when some of the record has been read and some cannot be: the unknown rows say UNAVAILABLE in their own cell, never a zero and never a blank.

#06

/WHITE INSERT

A control that lives on a card opens its slip over that card. The slip is not a second card: it is the same white insert, framed by the hairline that tells it apart from the page.

/THE CARDS AND THE CAP6

The three small surfaces: a hover card, a tooltip's cap and a tooltip's detail arm. The rule they print is the family's size rule - a cap for a mark, a slip for a document - and the two arms are shown side by side so the difference is a size, not a mood.

/THE MENUS13

The four list surfaces: a context menu, a dropdown, a menubar and the command palette. They are one instrument: the same register line, the same `[mark] [label] [meta]` row, the same five states, the same foot. The matrix, the contract and the rows read one file each: Content/Specimen/Overlay.ts states every cell's disposition and every row's state, and Component/UI/Overlay.tsx states the five dismissals once for the whole family. A condition added to the data appears on the matrix's figures and in the rows' order with no second edit - the same rule /THE FIELD follows. This band is the second about a family rather than a part, and it is here rather than on /THE SHEET for the same boundary: the sheet indexes the twelve Dynamic parts, and a band whose subject is the two seconds after a click cannot stand on a plate holding one part at 1:1.

One surface is not one component. The ten are ten behaviours - a drag, a hover, a right-click, a chord - and the claim this band makes is narrower and harder: that a reader cannot tell which primitive they are in by looking at the frame, only by what it does.

/THE DISPLAY

The display, and everything it is asked to hold

Nineteen components against twenty-one conditions: the matrix with a reason printed in full for every cell that cannot exist, the verdict on the two components no page mounts, the figure each condition earns, and then the family mounted live at every state it is best known by - a dense table, a strip with more tabs than fit, a disclosure with its panel open, a progress bar with a figure, a skeleton in the record grammar, and a month.

/WHAT THE DOCUMENT READS WITH12

The instruments the page carries its facts in: a table read across, a card that is one artifact, and the marks that name a claim. Every row here is a state of the same three parts, because the reading instruments are the ones whose adverse states nobody notices are missing.

The matrix, the verdicts and the rows read one file: Content/Specimen/Display.ts states every cell's disposition, both verdicts and every row's state. A condition added there appears on the matrix's figures, in the conditions' own list and in the rows' order with no second edit - the same rule /THE FIELD and /THE OVERLAY follow. This band is the third about a family rather than a part, and the first about the components the document only ever READS. That is why it carries a verdict section the other two do not need: Chart and Calendar are not mounted by any page, and a component that is neither used nor argued is a file waiting for someone.

Two cells cannot exist for the same reason in three different rows, and each one still carries its own sentence: a reason is a fact about that component, not a rule about the family. A cell that cannot exist is not a gap in the design - it is the design saying what it is not.

/THE RECORD

The record, and the combinations it never met

Eight components against twenty-four conditions: the matrix with a reason printed in full for every cell that cannot exist, the twelve behaviours the exploration produced with the cell that produced each, the three things this card found and did not fix, and then the family mounted live - one row, twenty rows, a key longer than its value, a value of three lines, a matrix of one column, a matrix of twelve, a rail where the two sides are equal, a trace with no events, an instrument with a missing reading, and the row grammar doing three things it could not do before: opening, marking and totalling.

/FACTS 22

What the document states as true, and what it states as compared. These are the two blocks a reader checks the project against.

# 52

THE FOUR CONSTRUCTORS

Register line

The shape itself: four questions, four answers - a set the block holds, a count it does not, a count that cannot be known, and a window of a larger set.

A SET THE BLOCK HOLDS, 08 # A SET THE BLOCK HOLDS / 08

A COUNT IT DOES NOT, 26 ROUTES # A COUNT IT DOES NOT / 26 ROUTES

A COUNT IT CANNOT KNOW, UNAVAILABLE # A COUNT IT CANNOT KNOW / UNAVAILABLE

A WINDOW OF A LARGER SET, 12 OF 240 # A WINDOW OF A LARGER SET / 12 OF 240

The matrix, the improvements and the rows read one file: Content/Specimen/Record.ts states every cell's disposition, every behaviour the exploration produced with the condition that produced it, the three observations this card did not fix, and every row's state. A condition added there appears on the matrix's figures, in the columns' own list and in the rows' order with no second edit - the same rule /THE FIELD, /THE OVERLAY and /THE DISPLAY follow. This band is the fourth about a family rather than a part, and the first whose subject is trust rather than use: a reader does not touch a ledger, they check the project against it. That is why its improvements section exists where the other three families' bands do not need one - a fact that has lost its adverse state is a fact that lies, and a lie is the one defect this family cannot survive.

Not one of these blocks ships a line of JavaScript. The ledger's disclosure is a `<details>`, the matrix is a `<table>`, the rail is an `<ol>` and the register is a `<p>` - so the band that prints every state they have costs the page nothing to mount, which is itself the claim.

/THE NARRATIVE

The narrative, and the states that reveal its frame

Fifteen components against nineteen conditions: the matrix with a reason printed in full for every cell that cannot exist, the twenty-three behaviours the exploration produced with the cell that produced each, the four things this card found and did not fix, and then the family mounted live - a band with a head and no body, an entry with a name and no claim, a stage with one step and a stage with nine, a run that stopped at its third step, a figure with no image and a figure whose caption is longer than its image, a well whose command overflows and a well of two hundred lines, a transcript with a failed turn, a pair with one empty pod, an archive with one entry and an archive with none, and a failure with no recovery path.
